key_insight: Layer importance splits into Necessity and Plasticity, and these two signals behave oppositely in transformers but overlap in Mamba-style state-space models.
engineering_relevance: For model compression, selective fine-tuning, and interpretability, the best layers to keep versus update may differ sharply between transformers and SSMs, so transfer of transformer heuristics is not guaranteed.
method: Measured Necessity by the loss increase when bypassing a layer in the pretrained model.
Measured Plasticity by the size of task-specific weight updates during fine-tuning.
Compared layer-importance patterns across residual transformers and Mamba-style SSMs, then linked them to forgetting under adaptation.
evidence_signal: Across evaluated residual transformers up to 14B parameters, Necessity and Plasticity anti-align with depth, while in evaluated Mamba-style SSMs they overlap; update concentration also changes catastrophic forgetting only in transformers.
watch_item: The findings are empirical for the evaluated model families and may not generalize to all SSM variants, tasks, or training setups without further validation.
paper_title: What Does Layer-Importance Reveal About Transformers and State-Space Models?
